kicker: BLACK FRIDAY HALF DAY · CLOSED 1:00PM ET · EVENING BRIEF
headline: Best week since April 2025 is in; perps ease 0.2% into the weekend.
lede: The S&P 500 ended Friday at 7,298.34, +1.61%, and +5.6% on the week, its strongest since April 2025 (AP). By 8:14pm the S&P perp was 7,290.95, −0.2% from the 1pm close, with the Nvidia perp −1.7%; futures reopen Sunday 6:00pm after OPEC+ meets.
drivers: Cash closes: Sandisk +15.96%, Micron +7.60%, WDC +7.22%, SOXX +4.76%, SMH +4.17%. Reuters: investors flocked back to hard hit AI shares; one strategist called the market oversold.
Nvidia +0.80% to $150.49 after opening near +2% (Yahoo). FT reported Thursday that Nvidia told server makers to halt AI server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries.
Reuters: traders almost fully price a December hike after Q3 GDP was revised to 4.3%. AP: the 10 year rose to 4.94% from 4.85% late Wednesday.
AP: about 4 of every 5 S&P 500 stocks rose and all 11 SPDR sector ETFs gained, led by tech XLK +2.80%. Reuters: volumes were thin after Thanksgiving.
picks: Perps since the 1pm close: S&P perp 7,290.95 vs 7,305.5 (−0.2%), Nasdaq 100 perp −0.3%, Nvidia −1.7%, Micron −1.8%, SK hynix −1.6%. No source explains the drift. Futures reopen Sunday 6:00pm.
Perps at 4:14pm: S&P perp 7,307.5, Nvidia perp 149.95. Little changed from the 1pm close.
Bonds closed: AP has the 10 year at 4.94% from 4.85% late Wednesday. Trading Economics: haven demand eased as tech rebounded and a December hike is priced.
VIX closed at 23.81, −2.99 (−11.2%) per Yahoo; down about 34% on the week from 35.89 on Nov 20 (Glass Desk).
Week: S&P +5.6%, its strongest since April 2025 (AP); Nasdaq +6.68%, Dow +5.47% (Glass Desk).
OPEC+ meets Sunday; Reuters reported it is expected to keep output targets unchanged through at least Q1 2027, not yet final (via Eurasia Business News). Known.
Close: S&P 7,298.34 (+1.61%), Nasdaq 24,129.50 (+2.31%), Dow 50,780.64 (+1.19%), per Reuters. All three posted weekly gains.
Memory led: Sandisk +15.96%, Micron +7.60%, WDC +7.22%, AMD +4.56%, SMH +4.17%. Nvidia +0.80% (Unusual Whales closes).
SPY made its session high, 729.15, in the final 5 minute bar.
Amazon up on strong Black Friday demand (Motley Fool); it closed +3.96%. Vertex fell about 5% after the FDA extended its kidney drug review (Reuters).
Session low: SPY 719.62 in the 10:05am bar; S&P day low 7,211.46 (Motley Fool data). Steady climb after.
Nvidia opened about 2% higher, then turned lower (Yahoo). FT reported Thursday it told Dell and Supermicro to halt AI server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia.
Reuters: traders almost fully price a Dec 9 hike. CME FedWatch was 98.9% Friday morning (Forbes). Already known.
Yields up: 10 year near 4.93%, 2 year near 4.70% in Reuters' late quotes. Bonds close 2:00pm.
means: S&P closed at 7,298, just above the final 7,294 OI gamma flip and under the 7,310 flow call wall.
SPXW options price ±1.00% for Monday, about 73 points; the S&P perp at 7,291 sits inside that range.
The VIX closed at 23.81, its lowest close of the week; a hold under 25 supports the rebound.
Back under 7,211, Friday's low, undoes the rebound; 7,183 is Wednesday's close.
calendar: ISM manufacturing (Nov) 55.2 consensus, prior 55.5. JOLTS 7.45M vs 7.523M prior. Fed's Bowman testifies
ADP (Nov) 80K consensus, prior 86K. Salesforce and Snowflake after close
Jobs (Nov): payrolls 90K consensus vs 165K prior, unemployment 4.1%

stories.what: S&P +5.6% on the week to 7,298.34, its strongest since April 2025 (AP). VIX closed at 23.81, −11.2% Friday and about −34% on the week.
stories.why: The rebound recovered about 60% of the prior week's 8.61% drop (Glass Desk); the Fed still looks set to hike Dec 9.
stories.read: Fear has eased fast, but yields kept rising.
stories.reacted: After the close the S&P perp eased to 7,290.95 at 8:14pm from 7,305.5 at 1pm, −0.2%.
stories.confirm: VIX stays under 25 and S&P holds 7,290 Monday.

stories.why: Chips led November's drop; Reuters says investors flocked back to hard hit AI shares.
stories.read: An oversold bounce led by the hardest hit names, on thin volume.
stories.reacted: SPY rose from a 719.62 low at 10:05am to a 729.15 high in the last bar. After hours the Micron perp is −1.8% and Sandisk −0.3% vs 1pm.
stories.confirm: Memory holds gains Monday and SMH stays above 435.

stories.h: Nvidia halts SE Asia server shipments
stories.what: FT: Nvidia told server makers including Dell and Supermicro to halt AI server deliveries to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia. A US rule on remote access to advanced chips took effect Nov 19.
stories.why: Nvidia's Singapore unit booked $104B of 2025 revenue (FT via TrendForce). It is unclear if the halt is temporary.
stories.read: Export rules now reach regional data center demand, not only China.
stories.reacted: First US session Friday: Nvidia opened near +2% and closed +0.80% at $150.49; the perp is −1.7% vs 1pm at 8:14pm. No source ties either move to the report.
stories.changes: Adds export risk to Nvidia's demand outlook; watch license guidance and Huang's Dec 3 testimony.
stories.confirm: Nvidia or Commerce confirms licensing delays.
stories.invalid: Shipments resume or licenses are granted quickly.

stories.what: TrendForce: limited demand visibility and supply chain caution raise the risk of DRAM contract price declines in 2028; procurement slowed slightly since early 4Q26.
stories.why: Memory pricing drives Micron, SK hynix and Samsung earnings.
stories.read: Long range caution, not a near term price cut.
stories.reacted: Memory stocks rallied anyway: Micron +7.60%, Sandisk +15.96%.

stories.what: Amazon closed +3.96% at $254.12; Motley Fool cites strong Black Friday demand.
stories.why: Consumer spending is a key read for Q4 growth with the Fed hiking.
stories.read: Holiday demand looks solid so far.
